connector: Jemmy and the prince have reached the river. Today they follow it toward the city, and Jemmy plans to give the prince the slip. Watch what the prince does on the mud flat, and what Jemmy does when he gets a ride.

plate.alt: A painting of a sailboat resting on wet sand and shallow water at low tide, under a gray sky
plate.credit: Trouville at Low Tide · Eugène Boudin, between 1888 and 1895 · Yale University Art Gallery · Public domain
plate.look: A harbor in France at low tide, painted by Eugène Boudin more than 125 years ago. When the tide goes out, the water drops and leaves wide, wet mud behind. In Chapter 15, Jemmy and the prince walk along a river mud flat at low tide.
plate.lookBtn: Tap to learn about this river painting

a.raw: she whistled a sharp note and pointed toward the road
a.fixed: She whistled a sharp note and pointed toward the road.
a.why: She starts the sentence, so it gets a capital S. A period ends it. Two actions joined by and need no comma.

b.raw: the old man cracked his whip and called to his horses
b.fixed: The old man cracked his whip and called to his horses.
b.why: The starts the sentence, so it gets a capital T. A period ends it. Two actions joined by and need no comma.

mfill1.h1: Say the two parts out loud, one right after the other.
mfill1.why: in + spect: to look closely into.

mfill2.h1: Put the ending right after spect. No space.
mfill2.why: spect + ator: one who looks on.

mfill3.h1: Put the first part right in front of spect. No space.
mfill3.why: re + spect: to look again, with care.

mfill4.h1: This one has three parts. Push all three together.
mfill4.why: in + spect + or: one whose job is to look.

vcloze1.h1: Read the vocabulary box. What does Jemmy call searching the mud?
vcloze1.why: mudlarking means searching river mud for things to sell.

vcloze2.h1: The boys walk below a raised bank beside the river. Which bank word means that?
vcloze2.why: an embankment is a raised bank beside a river.

vcloze3.h1: The birdcage is bent and old. Which bank word means beaten and worn out?

vcloze4.h1: Jemmy wants to sell it as firewood. Which bank word is wood from the river?
vcloze4.why: driftwood is wood washed up by the river.

gfill1.h1: It tells where. They go from one side of the stream to the other.
gfill1.why: They waded across the shallow stream.

gfill2.h1: It tells where. The footsteps are farther away than the trees.
gfill2.why: Footsteps came from beyond the trees.

gfill3.h1: It tells when. They got there while it was still light.
gfill3.why: They reached the hut before nightfall.

gfill4.h1: It tells how. Nobody heard him go.
gfill4.why: Jemmy slipped away without a sound.

match.mudlarking: Mudlarking is what Jemmy does on the mud flat. Look for the meaning about searching river mud.
match.embankment: An embankment is a place by the river. Look for the meaning about a raised bank.
match.battered: Battered describes something old and beaten up. Look for the meaning about worn out.
match.driftwood: Driftwood is wood. Look for the meaning about pieces the river washes up.

scholar.journal-q2: … and tell what the prince called Jemmy’s mudlarking at first.
scholar.journal-q3: … and tell what Jemmy calls the prince when he shouts to Captain Nips.

wordgame.winWeek: Jemmy dove into the hollow tree. Cutwater ran right past!

items.title: Pick the preposition
items.q: Jemmy rode ___ the coach with the potatoes.
items.why: Jemmy sat in the coach with the potatoes and the kettle. Inside fits.

miss.1: Under the coach is in the mud! Where did Jemmy sit?
miss.2: Beyond the coach is past it. Where did Jemmy sit?

items.title: Pick the preposition
items.q: The coach was stuck ___ a mud hole.
items.why: The wheels sank in the mud hole.

miss.1: Over would mean above it. The coach is stuck.
miss.2: After tells when. This sentence needs where.

items.title: Pick the preposition
items.q: The boys walked ___ the river toward the city.
items.why: They followed the river, walking beside it. Along fits.

miss.1: Into the river would get them wet! They walk beside it.
miss.2: Under the river? They walk beside it.

items.title: Pick the preposition
items.q: The prince pulled a chair leg ___ the mud.
items.why: He picked it up out of the mud. From fits.

miss.1: Into would push it down. He picks it up.
miss.2: Behind tells a place next to something. He picks it up out of the mud.

items.title: Build a spect word
items.why: spect + acle = spectacle, something big to look at.

miss.1: Speckle has no spect in it. Push spect and acle together.
miss.2: Spectator ends in ator. This one ends in acle.

items.title: Split it
items.why: pump · kin: the vowels are u and i, and the split goes between p and k.

items.title: Split it
items.why: sand · wich: two beats, and each one is easy to read.

items.title: Soft or hard?
items.q: Say giraffe. Is the g soft or hard?
items.why: The next letter is i, so the g is soft.

miss.1: Look at the letter after the g. It is i.

glossary.m: a boy kept in the castle to be punished whenever the prince does something wrong
money that kidnappers ask for before they let someone go
a small word in front of a noun that tells where, when, or how, like under, after, or with
the main part of a word. Other parts are added to the front or the end.
one beat in a word. Im-por-tant has three.
the last sentence of a paragraph. It says your big idea in a new way.
the opinion your paragraph sets out to prove

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it’s Opti. The boys made it to the river. Jemmy says he’ll give the prince the slip as soon as he can. But the river has treasure in its mud, and a rickety old coach is stuck nearby. As you read, keep your eye on the prince. He does something small, and it matters.
transcripts.guide1: Word work. Today you’ll build words with the root that means look, and you’ll pick the preposition that makes each sentence say what you mean. Then you’ll put long words back together, one beat at a time.
transcripts.guide2: Before you read: Chapter 15 starts on a mud flat by the river. Watch what Jemmy picks up, and what the prince picks up. Then a coach comes along. Watch Jemmy when it drives away.
transcripts.guide3: Real writers check their work before anyone else sees it. Today you’re the editor. Go through the checklist, one line at a time, and fix what you find.

notes.wordParts: The root spect means “look.” inspect = look closely into, spectator = one who looks on, respect = look again with care, inspector = one whose job is to look.
notes.grammar: A preposition sits in front of a noun and ties it to the sentence. It can tell where (under the straw), when (after the storm), or how (with great care).
notes.spelling: To read a long word, find the vowels, split between them, read each beat, then push the beats together: im·por·tant.
notes.wgrd: Good readers figure out what a character is like from the small things he does.
vocab: searching river mud for things to sell
a raised bank of earth beside a river
pieces of wood washed up by the river

mods.script: [warmly] Here's today's reading tip. Small things can tell you a lot about a character. On the mud flat in Chapter 15, watch what each boy picks up, and what each one says about it. What do those small moments show you? Then tap one of the two lenses below to use while you read. You don't need to write anything.

Two actions joined like that don't need a comma. Capital letter at the start, period at the end. Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or Sentence B, and type it the right way.

mods.todo: Say the parts out loud. Type the whole word in each box. Tap Check My Answers.
mods.script: Let's build one together. Pro, plus spect, plus or. Prospector! A person who looks for gold. The last word on your page has three parts too. Push all three together. Say each pair of parts out loud. Type the whole word in the box. Then tap Check My Answers.

mods.todo: Fill in each sentence with a word from the word bank. Tap Check My Work. Then play the matching game.
mods.script: When the prince asks Jemmy what he's doing in the mud, Jemmy answers with one word. Mudlarking! Mud, plus lark, which means to poke about. Read how we figured out the first word. Then fill in each sentence with a word from the word bank, and tap Check My Work. Last, play the matching game.

mods.todo: Tap Check yourself. Type a bank word in each blank. Tap Check My Answers. Then write two sentences.
mods.script: Same coach, three places. The coach rolled into the mud. Stuck! The coach rolled through the mud. It kept going. The coach rolled past the mud. It never touched it! Only one word changed. Now read each sentence below, and check the clue at the end: where, when, or how. Type the bank word that fits.

mods.todo: Clap the word. Then tap its chunks in order to build it.
mods.script: Here's a word in pieces. Tic. Fan. Tas. That's the wrong order! Clap it first: fan, tas, tic. Fantastic! Now tap the chunks in order. First, middle, last. If a chunk won't stick, try another one.

Think about this before you read. Jemmy says he'll give the prince the slip as soon as he can. He means it! But plans can change. Watch for the moment Jemmy looks back, and think about why he does what he does next.

mods.todo: Read the two questions. Then read Ch. 15 in your book.
mods.script: Time to read Chapter 15. First, read the two Pause and Think questions below. The tide is out, and the mud along the river has treasure in it, if you know where to look. Jemmy knows. Then a rickety old coach comes along. Stop at each question, think, and keep reading. After you read, do the Read Like a Writer box.

mods.todo: Pick Explorer or Scholar. Answer the three questions in full sentences.
mods.script: Now answer in full sentences, with details from the book. One, what is mudlarking, and why does Jemmy do it? Two, the prince picks up a broken chair leg and asks if it's worth anything. What does that small moment show? Three, what is Jemmy feeling when he sees the prince standing alone in the road? For a challenge, pick Scholar, and add one more detail to each answer.

mods.todo: Check your paragraph with the checklist. Write one mistake you fixed.
mods.script: Today you're the editor. Before anyone reads your paragraph, you check it. Go down the checklist one line at a time. Does every sentence start with a capital? Is there a comma before and, but, or so? Are names like Jemmy and Prince Brat capitalized? Fix what you find. Then write one mistake you fixed: what it was, and what it is now.

virtue.name: courage
virtue.title: Courage Watch: Did they show courage?

items.t: The prince calls Jemmy’s mudlarking “Trash” and walks on ahead.
items.why: Making fun of someone’s work is not courage.

items.t: Jemmy crawls over the embankment and asks a stranger, Captain Nips, for a ride.
items.why: He speaks up to a stranger to get where he needs to go.

items.t: Jemmy shouts, “Stop, Cap’n!” and has the coach wait for the prince.
items.why: He could ride away free, but he goes back for the prince.
